newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up on weather-related concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up on weather-related concerns.

text.p: Concerns that cool and dry weather might cut into hard red winter wheat production prompted a higher close in CBOT wheat futures Friday, traders and analysts said.
"A lot of the strength in the market today was in response to the drier conditions we're seeing in western Kansas," said Jason Roose, grain analyst with U.S. Commodities in West Des Moines, Iowa.
Traders said that the dry and cold weather forecast for much of the central U.S. Plains this weekend will only hinder the development of the already freeze-damaged wheat crop.
Temperatures overnight in portions of northwest Kansas and southwest Nebraska fell into the low 20s degrees Fahrenheit, according to U.S. meteorologists.
Some of Friday's gains were linked to short-covering before the U.S. Department of Agriculture releases winter wheat production estimates on Monday.
An average of analysts' estimates put total production at 1.574 billion bushels, hard red winter wheat production at 894.3 million, and soft red at 417.4 million.
CBOT wheat settled up three to 5-1/4 cents per bushel, with July up 4-3/4 at $4.13-3/4.
Firm hard red winter wheat basis levels were also cited as a source of Friday's strength, traders said.
Slow farmer selling has pushed levels higher over the last several days, and cash sources noted modest demand from wheat millers in the western Corn Belt.
On the day, Cargill bought 500,000 bushels July and one million bushels December. Smith Barney sold 800,000 July and 500,000 September, pit sources said.
In options trade, FIMAT sold 400 July $4.20 puts and Shatkin, Arbor and Karlov bought 200 July $4.50 calls, pit sources said.
Volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, versus Thursday's final volume of 18,781 contracts, according to CBOT data.
